$note: Size budgets for scripts/verify/hud-size.mjs (the hud-size CI job; `make gate-hud` locally). `measured` is what the tree produced on the day recorded; the budget is measured + tolerance_pct, and the gate fails on anything above it. Re-record with `node scripts/verify/hud-size.mjs --record` in the commit that legitimately changes a size, with the reason in the body; a number only ever moves with a reason. web_client_gzip is every .js/.css under aura-web/build/client gzipped and summed; web_client_largest_gzip the biggest single chunk; android_apk_debug the assembleDebug APK (R8 off, so release is the same size plus signing). Measure in a detached worktree at HEAD (git worktree add --detach <path> HEAD, symlink aura-web/node_modules in, build there): a build in /opt/jarvis measures every helper's uncommitted work in progress, not the branch, and the two differ by tens of kilobytes while a phase is in flight.

web_client_gzip.note_orb: Re-recorded 2026-09-09 for the 3D orb: 201.1 to 358.0 kB gzipped, +156.9. It is three.js, and it is one chunk of 143.3 kB. The orb brief requires a real WebGL sphere with torus rings and an icosphere core, so the renderer is the cost of the feature rather than an oversight. Measured at HEAD in a detached worktree as the note above requires. The Orb is a DYNAMIC import and this number does not reflect that, deliberately: web_client_gzip sums every emitted file, so a split moves bytes out of the first download without moving them out of the build -- the same thing already noted for the capability map. What the split buys is a correct first paint (the 2D reactor renders until the chunk lands) and a working HUD on a machine with no WebGL; it buys nothing here. If this has to come down, the honest levers are dropping three.js for a hand-rolled WebGL layer, or shipping the orb only to surfaces that will use it -- not another split.

web_client_largest_gzip.note: The largest chunk is the HUD route (src/routes/[...path]) since wave 3: the one page of the console, carrying the host, the twenty-one bodies, the data layer and the settings catalogue. Re-recorded from 28.0 kB with that reason: before the migration the largest chunk was one of seventeen routes and the gate protected against a route swallowing a library; now there is one route and it is the product, so what the gate protects against is that route growing past what it carries today. The gallery's chunk is second (its ?hud=1 demo is still fetched, not bundled). Re-recorded again on 2026-09-06 for Reactor II wave 1 (36.3 → 38.8 kB): the top bar, the dock and the stage are the route's now, and the material's blur budget, parallax and scrim left the shared chunk, which is why the total moved only 2.8 kB. Re-recorded on 2026-09-07 for the room with no tabs (38.8 → 41.3 kB): the launcher, the settings menu, the task ring and the running view are all this one route's, and the tab strip they replaced was 1.2 kB of it. The TOTAL fell 6.2 kB in the same change — what left the bundle is the settings panel's second copy of the catalogue renderer and the eight route-to-layout tables. Re-recorded on 2026-09-08 for v3 (41.3 to 43.0 kB): the map and the three new bodies, less the capability map, which moved out of this chunk into a fetch and took 5.0 kB with it — the chunk measured 48.0 kB before that change and 43.0 after.
